chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G1

words.ex: He is an apprentice in a car repair shop.
words.ex_cn: 他是汽车修理店的一名学徒。
words.en: An apprentice is a young person who works for someone in order to learn their skill.

words.ex: He has a natural aptitude for math.
words.ex_cn: 他天生有数学天赋。
words.en: An aptitude is a natural ability to do something.

words.ex: The craftsman made a wooden chair by hand.
words.ex_cn: 这位工匠手工制作了一把木椅。
words.en: A craftsman is a skilled worker who makes things by hand.

words.ex: The surgeon's dexterity saved the patient's life.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生的灵巧救了病人的命。
words.en: Skill and grace in physical movement, especially in the use of the hands; adroitness.

words.ex: He is adroit at fixing broken machines.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长修理坏掉的机器。
words.en: Someone who is adroit is quick and skillful in their thoughts, behavior, or actions.

words.ex: He is ambidextrous and can write with both hands.
words.ex_cn: 他是左右手都灵巧的，可以用两只手写字。
words.en: Someone who is ambidextrous can use both their right and left hands equally well.

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G2

words.ex: He lived in indigence after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Indigence is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: He tries to economize by walking to work.
words.ex_cn: 他通过步行上班来节省开支。
words.en: To economize means to use less money, time, or resources than usual in order to save them.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.ex: He is frugal with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很节俭。
words.en: If you describe someone as frugal, you mean that they are careful about spending money and use things only when they need to.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G3

words.ex: His avarice knew no bounds, always seeking more wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他的贪婪无止境，总是追求更多的财富。
words.en: Avarice is extremely strong desire for money and possessions.

words.ex: Her family gave a dowry when she married.
words.ex_cn: 她结婚时，她的家人给了嫁妆。
words.en: A dowry is property or money that a woman brings to her husband when they marry.

words.tr:
v. 意思是说；表示…的意思；
n. 手段；方法；收入；
words.ex: This sign means you cannot park here.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志意思是说这里不能停车。
words.en: Means refers to a method or way of doing something, or the resources or assets available for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The palace showed opulence with golden walls and silk curtains.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿以金墙和丝绸窗帘展现了富裕。
words.en: Opulence is great wealth or luxuriousness.

words.ex: He covets his neighbor's car.
words.ex_cn: 他垂涎邻居的车。
words.en: If you covet something, you have a very strong desire to possess it, especially something that belongs to someone else.

words.tr:
n. 羊毛；一只羊一次剪下的毛
vt. 剪下羊毛；敲诈；诈取
words.ex: The sheep is losing its fleece in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这只羊在春天掉毛。
words.en: Fleece can refer to the wool coat of a sheep or similar animal, or to a soft fabric made from this wool. As a verb, it means to shear the wool from a sheep or to swindle someone.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.ex: The affluent family bought a big house by the lake.
words.ex_cn: 这个富裕的家庭在湖边买了一栋大房子。
words.en: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.

words.ex: He works in financial planning.
words.ex_cn: 他从事财政规划工作。
words.en: Relating to finance or the management of large amounts of money.

words.tr:
adj. 奢侈的；慷慨给予的；挥霍的；过多的
v. 浪费；挥霍；慷慨给予
words.ex: He threw a lavish party for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的生日举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: If you describe something as lavish, you mean that it is very elaborate and impressive and a lot of money has been spent on it. If you say that someone is lavish in the way they behave, you mean that they give, spend, or use a lot of something.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G4

words.tr: adj. 懦弱的；毫无志气的；
words.ex: He was craven and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as craven, you are criticizing them for being very cowardly.

words.ex: He felt trepidation before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试前感到恐惧。
words.en: A feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen.

words.ex: The dog cowers when the thunder sounds.
words.ex_cn: 当雷声响起时，狗会蜷缩起来。
words.en: To crouch down in fear.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: He is apprehensive about the test.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试感到担忧。
words.en: Anxious or fearful that something bad or unpleasant will happen.

words.tr: adj. 胆小而恶毒的；卑鄙的
words.ex: The dastardly thief stole the money at night.
words.ex_cn: 那个卑鄙的贼在夜里偷了钱。
words.en: If you describe an action as dastardly, you mean it is wicked and intended to harm someone.

words.ex: The timid boy whispered his answer.
words.ex_cn: 这个害羞的男孩小声说出了他的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or actions as timid, you are criticizing them for being too cautious or slow to act, because they are nervous about the possible consequences of their actions.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G5

words.ex: He exploited the situation to get more money.
words.ex_cn: 他利用这个情况赚了更多钱。
words.en: To exploit someone or something means to use them in a way that benefits you, often unfairly or without considering their rights or feelings. It can also refer to the act of making full use of and deriving benefit from a resource.

words.ex: He showed great fortitude during the hard times.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰难时期展现了极大的毅力。
words.en: Fortitude is the mental and emotional strength that enables a person to face difficulty, danger, or pain without fear.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；鲁莽的；大胆创新的
words.ex: He made an audacious plan to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他制定了一个大胆的计划，独自攀登那座山。
words.en: If you describe someone as audacious, you mean that they take risks in order to achieve something and show a willingness to challenge conventional ideas.

words.tr: adj. 勇敢的；无所畏惧的；不屈不挠的
words.ex: The dauntless firefighter ran into the burning building.
words.ex_cn: 这位无畏的消防员冲进了着火的建筑。
words.en: If you describe someone as dauntless, you mean they are not easily frightened or discouraged from doing something.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；百折不挠的
words.ex: He is indomitable in facing challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他在面对挑战时永不言败。
words.en: If you say that someone has an indomitable spirit, you admire them because they never give up or admit that they have been defeated.

words.tr: adj. 有勇气的，大胆的; n. （Plucky）（印、英、中国香港）普拉琦（人名）
words.ex: She showed a plucky determination to overcome her fears.
words.ex_cn: 她表现出了克服恐惧的勇敢决心。
words.en: Having or showing courage and spirit in trying circumstances.

words.tr: n. 大量同时出现的事件；
words.ex: There was a rash of burglaries last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月发生了一连串的盗窃案。
words.en: If someone is rash or does rash things, they act without thinking carefully first, and therefore make mistakes or behave foolishly.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G6

words.tr:
n. 别名；化名
adv. 又被称为；另外地
words.ex: He uses an alias to hide his real name.
words.ex_cn: 他使用一个化名来隐藏他的真实姓名。
words.en: An alias is a false or assumed identity, especially one used by a criminal.

words.ex: The ancient symbol remains an enigma.
words.ex_cn: 这个古代符号仍然是一个谜。
words.en: An enigma is something that is mysterious and difficult to understand.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.ex: He likes to seclude himself in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢把自己 secluded 在森林里。
words.en: To seclude means to keep someone away from other people, or to keep something away from other things.

words.tr: adj. 秘密的；暗中行事的
words.ex: He made a clandestine meeting with his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他与朋友进行了一次秘密会面。
words.en: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.tr: adj. 偷偷摸摸的；不声张的；秘密的
words.ex: The thief moved with stealthy steps.
words.ex_cn: 小偷蹑手蹑脚地移动。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as stealthy, you mean that they are quiet and secret in what they do, often because they do not want to be seen or heard.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G7

words.ex: The candidate's avowal of support for the new policy was met with mixed reactions.
words.ex_cn: 候选人公开支持新政策的声明引起了褒贬不一的反应。
words.en: An avowal is a statement in which you say or admit something that you believe, support, or intend to do.

words.ex: He apprised her of the change.
words.ex_cn: 他通知了她这个变化。
words.en: If you are apprised of something, someone tells you about it.

words.ex: He won't divulge the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他不会泄露这个秘密。
words.en: If you divulge a piece of secret or private information, you tell it to someone.

words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.ex: The teacher will enlighten the students about the truth.
words.ex_cn: 老师将向学生们阐明真相。
words.en: To enlighten someone means to give them more knowledge and greater understanding about something.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G8

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: The book has a compact design.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的设计很紧凑。
words.en: A compact object or substance is small and dense, with all its parts closely packed together.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.tr: v. 同意；继承；即位；加入
words.ex: He acceded to their request.
words.ex_cn: 他同意了他们的请求。
words.en: If you accede to someone's request, you do what they ask.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.ex: The number of apples corresponds to the number of oranges.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的数量与橙子的数量相对应。
words.en: If one thing corresponds to another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one is the cause or the result of the other.

words.tr: vt. 用鸠尾榫接合；与……吻合; vi. 吻合; n. 楔形榫头
words.ex: The carpenter carefully dovetailed the pieces of wood together.
words.ex_cn: 木匠仔细地将木片用鸠尾榫接合在一起。
words.en: If two things dovetail or if one thing dovetails with another, the two things fit together neatly or have some common characteristics.

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.tr: v. 发慈悲；动怜悯心；缓和
words.ex: The teacher finally relented and gave the students more time.
words.ex_cn: 老师终于发慈悲，给了学生们更多时间。
words.en: If you relent, you allow someone to do something that you had previously refused to allow them to do.

words.tr: adj. 兼容的；可和谐共存的；
words.ex: This printer is compatible with my computer.
words.ex_cn: 这个打印机与我的电脑兼容。
words.en: If things, for example, systems, ideas, and beliefs, are compatible, they work well together or can exist together successfully.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G9

words.ex: They had an altercation over the parking space.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为停车空间发生了争吵。
words.en: An altercation is a noisy argument or disagreement, especially in public.

words.ex: The glass showed a clear cleavage after it fell.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃掉落后出现了明显的裂纹。
words.en: Cleavage refers to the act of splitting or dividing something, especially along a natural line or grain. It can also refer to the space between a woman's breasts, especially as revealed by a low-cut garment.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: There is friction between the two neighbors over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居因为篱笆问题产生了不和。
words.en: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

words.ex: He is facing litigation over the contract.
words.ex_cn: 他因合同问题面临诉讼。
words.en: Litigation is the process of taking legal action or bringing a lawsuit in a court of law.

words.ex: He tries not to antagonize his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他尽量不惹恼他的弟弟。
words.en: To antagonize someone means to cause them to feel hostile or unfriendly towards you.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.tr: v. 使卷入；使陷入；牵连
words.ex: He didn't want to embroil his friend in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他不想让朋友卷入这场争吵。
words.en: To involve someone in a difficult or complicated situation.

words.ex: He estranged his brother with harsh words.
words.ex_cn: 他用刻薄的话与兄弟疏远了。
words.en: If you estrange someone, especially a member of your family, you cause them to stop being friendly or close to you.

words.tr:
v. 争论；争执；吵架
n. 争吵；口角
words.ex: They wrangle over the price every day.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天为价格争执。
words.en: If you wrangle with someone, you argue with them in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr: adj. 不能调和的；无法化解的；不兼容的
words.ex: Their views are irreconcilable.
words.ex_cn: 他们的观点无法调和。
words.en: If two things such as opinions or proposals are irreconcilable, they are so different from each other that it is not possible to believe or have both of them.

words.tr: 短语. 有分歧的；不一致的；与...相矛盾
words.ex: The two accounts are at variance with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个说法彼此不一致。
words.en: If one thing is at variance with another, the two things are different or inconsistent with each other.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G10

words.ex: She added ketchup as a condiment to her fries.
words.ex_cn: 她把番茄酱当作调味品加在薯条上。
words.en: A condiment is a substance such as salt, pepper, or mustard that you add to food when you eat it in order to improve the flavor.

words.ex: He is a glutton who eats too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他是个贪吃糖的暴食者。
words.en: A glutton is a person who eats and drinks excessively or voraciously.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.ex: The cool water helped to slake his thirst.
words.ex_cn: 清凉的水帮助他解渴。
words.en: If you slake a thirst, desire, or need, you satisfy it.

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

words.tr: adj. 美味的；甘美的；满足感官的；性感的
words.ex: The fruit was luscious and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这种水果甘甜可口。
words.en: If you describe something as luscious, you mean that it is very pleasant to taste, smell, look at, or listen to.

words.ex: The soup was palatable after adding salt.
words.ex_cn: 加了盐后，汤变得可口美味了。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as palatable, you mean that it tastes pleasant.

words.ex: The cactus has succulent leaves to store water.
words.ex_cn: 仙人掌有多汁的叶子来储存水分。
words.en: (of food) tender, juicy, and tasty; (of a plant) having thick, fleshy tissues adapted to water storage.

words.tr: adj. 贪吃的；贪婪的；如饥似渴的
words.ex: He is a voracious eater who finishes all the food on his plate.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个贪吃的人，总会把盘子里的所有食物吃完。
words.en: If you describe a person or their appetite for something as voracious, you mean that they want a lot of something.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G11

words.tr: n. 全部；全范围；全音阶；音域
words.ex: The gamut of human emotions was on display during the performance.
words.ex_cn: 表演中展现了人类情感的全部范围。
words.en: The gamut of something is the complete range of things of that kind, or a scale that includes all the notes in a musical octave.

words.ex: He didn't care about an iota of the details.
words.ex_cn: 他对这些细节的极小量都不在意。
words.en: An iota is an extremely small amount of something.

words.ex: The magnitude of this decision will affect everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定的重要性会影响每个人。
words.en: Magnitude refers to the great size or extent of something, or the importance of something.

words.tr: n. 微薄的工资；极少的报酬
words.ex: He lived on a pittance during his early career.
words.ex_cn: 他在职业生涯初期靠微薄的收入生活。
words.en: A very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone as an allowance or wage.

words.ex: The superabundance of fruit in the market made prices drop significantly.
words.ex_cn: 市场上水果的过多供应使得价格大幅下降。
words.en: An amount that is more than is needed or can be used.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: The statue was colossal, taller than the building.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像巨大，比大楼还高。
words.en: If you describe something as colossal, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.ex: The house has a commodious living room.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个宽敞的客厅。
words.en: A commodious room or building is large and has a lot of space.

words.ex: The universe may be infinite.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙可能是无限的。
words.en: If you describe something as infinite, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in amount or degree.

words.ex: The difference between the two values is infinitesimal.
words.ex_cn: 这两个值之间的差异极微。
words.en: Something that is infinitesimal is extremely small.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.tr: adj. （非正式）不值钱的；眼光狭小的；微不足道的; n. 价值低微的小硬币；西班牙小币；（非正式...
words.ex: He dismissed her concerns as picayune.
words.ex_cn: 他不屑一顾地认为她的担忧微不足道。
words.en: If you describe something as picayune, you mean that it is very small, unimportant, or trivial.

words.ex: He is puny and can't lift the box.
words.ex_cn: 他很瘦弱，举不起那个箱子。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as puny, you mean that they are small and weak.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G12

words.ex: His infirmity made it hard to walk.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱使他走路困难。
words.en: An infirmity is a physical or mental weakness.

words.ex: The illness debilitates him every winter.
words.ex_cn: 每年冬天，这场疾病都会使他虚弱。
words.en: To make someone weak and infirm.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.ex: The injury incapacitated him for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤使他几周无法行动。
words.en: To make someone unable to do something, especially because of injury or illness.

words.tr: adj. 堕落的；颓废的；衰落的
words.ex: He ate a decadent chocolate cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块奢华的巧克力蛋糕。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as decadent, you think that they are morally corrupt or that they are living in an immoral way.

words.tr: adj. 衰老的；老朽的；破旧的
words.ex: The old house is decrepit and needs repair.
words.ex_cn: 这栋老房子破旧不堪，需要修理。
words.en: Something that is decrepit is old and in poor condition.

words.ex: The old house looked dilapidated after years of neglect.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子因多年疏于维护而显得残破。
words.en: A building that is dilapidated is old and in a generally bad condition.

words.tr:
adj. 轻而薄的；易坏的；不足信的
n. 复写纸；薄纸副本
words.ex: The flimsy chair broke when he sat on it.
words.ex_cn: 那把脆弱的椅子当他坐上去时就断了。
words.en: Something that is flimsy is not very strong or solid, and therefore easily damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: The old man is frail and needs help to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人瘦弱，需要帮助才能走路。
words.en: Someone who is frail is not very strong or healthy.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G13

words.tr: n. 堡垒；防御工事；保障
words.ex: The new law serves as a bulwark against corruption.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律起到了防止腐败的作用。
words.en: A bulwark is a wall built for defence, especially one that is part of a larger fortification system.

words.ex: The old citadel stands on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 古老的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: A citadel is a fortress, typically on high ground, protecting or dominating a city.

words.tr:
n. 专长；特长
adv. 用强音
words.ex: His forte is playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他的强项是弹钢琴。
words.en: A thing at which someone excels.

words.ex: He runs with great vigour every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都充满精力地跑步。
words.en: Physical or mental strength and energy.

words.tr: v. 增添活力；振奋；使活跃
words.ex: The fresh air invigorates me every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早晨的新鲜空气让我精神焕发。
words.en: If something invigorates you, it makes you feel more energetic and alive.

words.tr: adj. 有说服力的；令人信服的
words.ex: His argument was cogent and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点有说服力且容易理解。
words.en: A cogent argument, reason, etc. is clearly expressed and persuades people to believe it.

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.ex: The storm was formidable and destroyed many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴很可怕，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as formidable, you mean that you feel slightly frightened by them because they are very great or impressive.

words.tr: adj. 坚不可摧的；不可战胜的
words.ex: The castle was impregnable during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡在战争期间固若金汤。
words.en: An impregnable building or place is so strong and secure that it cannot be entered or captured by force.

words.tr: adj. 强健的；强壮的；结实的；
words.ex: The dog is robust and runs every day.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗很强健，每天跑步。
words.en: Strong and healthy; vigorous. (of an object) sturdy in construction.

words.tr: adj. 紧握的；顽强的；坚决的；强的（记忆力）
words.ex: The child held the toy with tenacious hands.
words.ex_cn: 孩子用紧握的手抓住玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as tenacious, you are admiring their determination to do something and their refusal to stop trying even when it is difficult.

words.ex: He gave a vehement reply to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了激烈的回答。
words.en: If a person or their actions or comments are vehement, the person has very strong feelings or opinions and expresses them forcefully.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G14

words.ex: The default setting is on.
words.ex_cn: 默认设置是开启的。
words.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying a debt or keeping to an agreement, they fail to do it.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.ex: His neglect of the project caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 他对项目的疏忽导致了延误。
words.en: If you neglect someone or something, you fail to give them the attention or care that they need.

words.tr: adj. 不留心的；不注意的
words.ex: He was heedless of the warning signs.
words.ex_cn: 他对警告信号毫不在意。
words.en: If you are heedless of someone or something, you do not take any notice of them.

words.tr: adj. 不注意的；疏忽的；非故意的
words.ex: He made an inadvertent mistake while typing.
words.ex_cn: 他在打字时不小心犯了个错误。
words.en: If something bad is inadvertent, it is done without realizing that it is wrong or that it could have bad consequences.

words.tr: adj. 疏忽的；怠慢的；不留心的
words.ex: It would be remiss of me not to mention the importance of regular exercise.
words.ex_cn: 不提及定期锻炼的重要性，我会感到疏忽。
words.en: If someone is remiss, they are careless and do not do the things they are expected to do.

words.tr: adj. 不修边幅的；邋遢的
words.ex: He wore slovenly clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿着邋遢的衣服去上班。
words.en: If you describe someone as slovenly, you disapprove of them because they are careless and untidy in their appearance or habits.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G15

words.ex: Her eyes showed her deep solicitude for him.
words.ex_cn: 她眼中的深情显示了她对他的深切关怀。
words.en: Solicitude is care or concern for someone or something.

words.ex: The guard showed vigilance during the night shift.
words.ex_cn: 守卫在夜班期间保持警惕。
words.en: Vigilance is the action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger or difficulties.

words.tr:
v. 注意；留心
n. 注意；留心
words.ex: He did not heed the warning.
words.ex_cn: 他没有理会那个警告。
words.en: If you heed someone's advice or warning, you pay attention to it and do what they suggest.

words.tr: v. 详细检查；仔细察看
words.ex: The teacher scrutinizes every student's homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师仔细检查每位学生的作业。
words.en: If you scrutinize something, you examine it very carefully, often to find out some information from it or about it.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: He is scrupulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他检查作业时一丝不苟。
words.en: If you are scrupulous, you are careful, thorough, and extremely attentive to details.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G16

words.ex: The denizen of the forest knows all the paths.
words.ex_cn: 森林的居民知道所有的路。
words.en: A denizen of a particular place is someone who lives there or is often there.

words.ex: His domicile is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他的住所位于纽约。
words.en: A domicile is the place where a person lives or has their home.

words.tr: n. （医院或监狱中的）同宿者；监犯
words.ex: The inmate shared his cell with two others.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯和另外两个人共用一间牢房。
words.en: A person who is confined in a prison, hospital, or other institution.

words.tr:
adj. 本土的；
n. 土著；本地人；
words.ex: This plant is native to Australia.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物原产于澳大利亚。
words.en: A native of a particular country or region is someone who was born in that country or region.

words.tr: n. 游牧民；流浪者；游牧生活；流浪生活
words.ex: The nomad walks with his sheep across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 游牧民带着他的羊群穿越沙漠。
words.en: A nomad is someone who has no permanent home and moves according to the seasons from place to place in search of food, water, and grazing land.

words.ex: His sojourn in Paris lasted two years.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎旅居了两年。
words.en: A sojourn is a temporary stay in a place.

words.tr:
n. 通勤；
v. 通勤；
words.ex: His daily commute takes an hour by train.
words.ex_cn: 他每天的通勤坐火车要一个小时。
words.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

words.ex: Birds migrate south in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天迁徙到南方。
words.en: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

words.ex: The nomadic family moves with their sheep every season.
words.ex_cn: 这个游牧家庭每季都随着羊群迁移。
words.en: A nomadic way of life is one in which people move from place to place instead of living in one place all the time.

words.ex: He went abroad to study medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他去国外学医。
words.en: In or to a foreign country or countries.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G17

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

words.ex: He got a fine for a small infraction.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个小违规行为被罚款。
words.en: An infraction is a violation or infringement of a law, agreement, or set of rules.

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.ex: The insurrection failed because people did not support it.
words.ex_cn: 这次起义失败了，因为人们不支持它。
words.en: An insurrection is a violent uprising against an authority or government.

words.tr:
adj. 不满的；不服的
n. 不满现状的人；反抗者
words.ex: The malcontent workers complained about low pay.
words.ex_cn: 不满的员工抱怨工资太低。
words.en: A malcontent is a person who is dissatisfied and rebellious.

words.tr: n. 煽动叛乱的言论（或行动）
words.ex: He was arrested for sedition against the government.
words.ex_cn: 他因煽动叛乱反对政府而被逮捕。
words.en: Sedition is the act of encouraging people to oppose or fight against the authority of a state or monarch.

words.ex: He was punished for transgressing the law.
words.ex_cn: 他因违法而受到惩罚。
words.en: To transgress means to go beyond the limits of what is morally, socially, or legally acceptable.

words.tr:
v. 非法侵入；侵扰；冒犯
n. 非法进入；冒犯
words.ex: He trespasses on private land.
words.ex_cn: 他擅自进入私人土地。
words.en: To trespass is to enter someone's land or property without their permission.

words.ex: The student was insubordinate to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这名学生对老师不服从。
words.en: If someone is insubordinate, they deliberately do not obey someone of higher rank.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；任性的；乖张的；故意作对的；悖理的
words.ex: He gave a perverse answer to the simple question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个简单的问题给出了一个反常的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone as perverse, you mean that they deliberately behave in an unreasonable way, especially by doing the opposite of what is expected or wanted.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G18

words.ex: He swore allegiance to his country.
words.ex_cn: 他向自己的国家宣誓效忠。
words.en: Loyalty or commitment to a superior or to a group or cause.

words.ex: He acquiesced to his boss's decision.
words.ex_cn: 他默许了老板的决定。
words.en: If you acquiesce in something, you agree to do what someone wants or to accept what they do even though you may not agree with it.

words.ex: He will defer his trip until next month.
words.ex_cn: 他将把旅行推迟到下个月。
words.en: If you defer an event or action, you arrange for it to happen at a later date, rather than immediately or at the previously planned time.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.ex: The docile dog followed its owner quietly.
words.ex_cn: 这只温顺的狗安静地跟着主人。
words.en: A docile person or animal is quiet, not aggressive, and easily controlled.

words.ex: The meek boy quietly listened to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个温顺的男孩静静地听老师讲课。
words.en: If you describe a person as meek, you think that they are gentle and quiet, and likely to do what other people say.

words.ex: The plastic is pliable and easy to bend.
words.ex_cn: 这种塑料柔韧，容易弯曲。
words.en: A pliable object or material is easy to bend or shape without breaking.

words.tr: adj. 易驾驭的；温顺的；易处理的
words.ex: The dog is so tractable that it follows commands effortlessly.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗非常驯良，能轻松地服从命令。
words.en: If you say that a person, problem, or device is tractable, you mean that they can be easily controlled or dealt with.

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G19

words.ex: He dawdled away the afternoon at the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园里混掉了整个下午。
words.en: If you dawdle, you spend more time than is necessary going somewhere or doing something.

words.ex: He always procrastinates doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他总是拖延做作业。
words.en: If you procrastinate, you keep leaving things you should do until later, often because you do not want to do them.

words.ex: He tries to protract the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他试图延长会议。
words.en: To protract something means to make it last longer than usual or necessary, often in a way that is annoying or inconvenient.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: Two events happen concurrently.
words.ex_cn: 两个事件同时发生。
words.en: Happening or existing at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.tr: adj. 多年生的；反复出现的；
words.ex: These perennial flowers bloom every year.
words.ex_cn: 这些多年生的花每年都会开花。
words.en: A perennial plant is one that lives for more than two years, often flowering and producing seeds multiple times over its lifespan.

words.tr: adj. 不定时发生的；时有时无的；零星的
words.ex: He makes sporadic visits to his grandparents.
words.ex_cn: 他时不时去看望他的祖父母。
words.en: occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places; scattered or isolated

chapters.name: 第一章 中心思想 G20

words.ex: The essence of love is caring for others.
words.ex_cn: 爱的本质是关心他人。
words.en: The essence of something is its basic and most important characteristic which gives it its individual identity.

words.ex: You need basic math as a prerequisite for this course.
words.ex_cn: 你学习这门课程的前提是掌握基础数学。
words.en: A prerequisite is something that must exist or happen before something else can exist or happen.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: The rain necessitated staying indoors.
words.ex_cn: 下雨使待在室内成为必需。
words.en: To necessitate something means to make it necessary for something to be done or to happen.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.ex: This tool can obviate the need for manual work.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具可以避免手动工作的需要。
words.en: To obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, especially so that action to deal with it becomes unnecessary.

words.ex: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是必须的。
words.en: If something is compulsory, you must do it because of a rule or law.

words.tr: adj. 无故的；无必要的；无偿的；免费的
words.ex: He made a gratuitous comment about her clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的衣服做了毫无必要的评论。
words.en: If you describe something as gratuitous, you mean that it is unnecessary, and often harmful or upsetting.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.tr: adj. 在职的；负有义务的；
words.ex: The incumbent mayor won the election again.
words.ex_cn: 现任市长再次赢得了选举。
words.en: An incumbent is someone who currently holds a particular office or position, especially in politics. It can also refer to something that is necessary as a duty or responsibility.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.tr: adj. 紧迫的； v. 按；“press”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pressing issue is finding clean water.
words.ex_cn: 紧迫的问题是找到干净的水。
words.en: If something is pressing, it needs to be dealt with immediately because it is important or urgent.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G1

words.ex: He wrote his autobiography when he was 70.
words.ex_cn: 他70岁时写了自传。
words.en: An autobiography is a book about the life of a person, written by that person.

words.ex: The autocrat rules the country with no elections.
words.ex_cn: 独裁者在没有选举的情况下统治国家。
words.en: An autocrat is a ruler who has absolute power.

words.tr:
n. 亲笔签名；亲笔稿
v. 亲笔签名于；亲笔书写
words.ex: He asked the singer for an autograph.
words.ex_cn: 他向歌手要了一张签名。
words.en: An autograph is a person's own signature, especially that of a famous person, or a manuscript in the author's own handwriting.

words.ex: The factory uses automation to make cars.
words.ex_cn: 工厂使用自动化来制造汽车。
words.en: The use of largely automatic equipment in a system of manufacturing or other production process.

words.tr: n. 自动装置；机器人；机器人似的人
words.ex: The factory was filled with automatons that performed repetitive tasks.
words.ex_cn: 工厂里满是执行重复任务的自动机。
words.en: An automaton is a machine that operates on its own without the need for human control, especially a robot in the form of a human.

words.tr: n. 自主权；自治权；自治；
words.ex: The region demands autonomy from the central government.
words.ex_cn: 该地区要求从中央政府获得自主权。
words.en: Autonomy is the ability or condition of being self-governing; independence in one's thoughts or actions.

words.ex: The doctor did an autopsy to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 医生做了尸检以查明死因。
words.en: An autopsy is a medical examination of a dead body to discover the cause of death.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.ex: The door opens automatically when you get close.
words.ex_cn: 当你靠近时，门会自动打开。
words.en: If something happens automatically, it happens as a part of the normal process or system, without needing to be started by someone.

words.tr: adj. 自治的；有自治权的；自主的；
words.ex: The region has autonomous control over its education system.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区对其教育系统拥有自治权。
words.en: An autonomous organization, country, or region is independent and has the freedom to govern itself.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G2

words.tr: n. 贵族政治；贵族统治；贵族
words.ex: The aristocracy lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族住在巨大的城堡里。
words.en: The highest class in certain societies, especially those holding hereditary titles or offices.

words.tr: n. 专制制度；独裁制度；专制国家
words.ex: The autocracy was overthrown by a popular revolution.
words.ex_cn: 独裁政府被一场民众革命推翻了。
words.en: Autocracy is a system of government in which a country is ruled by a person or group with total power.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.ex: People vote in democracy to choose their leaders.
words.ex_cn: 人们在民主制度下投票选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.

words.tr: n. 富豪；财阀；财阀政治；富豪统治
words.ex: The country is often criticized for being a plutocracy where wealth determines political power.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家经常因为财富决定政治权力的富豪统治而受到批评。
words.en: A plutocracy is a society or system that is ruled or controlled by people of great wealth or income.

words.tr: n. 专家治国制度；技术官僚政治；技术专家政府
words.ex: The country is ruled by a technocracy of engineers and scientists.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群工程师和科学家统治。
words.en: A technocracy is a system of governance where decision-makers are selected on the basis of their expertise in a given area of responsibility, particularly with regard to scientific or technical knowledge.

words.ex: The aristocrat lived in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 这位贵族住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: An aristocrat is a person of high rank in a society, especially one who inherits a title and lands.

words.tr: n. 民主主义者；民主党员；
words.ex: He is a democrat who believes in equal rights for all.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位相信所有人平等权利的民主主义者。
words.en: A democrat is someone who believes in the principles of democracy, such as the idea that everyone should have an equal say in how their country is governed.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G3

words.tr: n. 煽动者；蛊惑民心的政客
words.ex: The politician is a demagogue who uses angry words to win votes.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客是一个煽动者，用愤怒的言辞赢得选票。
words.en: A demagogue is a political leader who seeks support by appealing to popular desires and prejudices rather than by using rational argument.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: The internet helps to democratize access to information.
words.ex_cn: 互联网有助于使信息获取更加普及。
words.en: To make something accessible to everyone, especially something that was previously restricted to a particular group of people.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G4

words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.tr: n. 喧嚣；大混乱；大吵大闹
words.ex: The crowd created pandemonium when the winner was announced.
words.ex_cn: 当获胜者被宣布时，人群陷入了混乱。
words.en: Pandemonium is a situation in which there is a lot of noise and confusion because people are excited, angry, or frightened.

words.tr: n. 巨大的数量（或收藏品）
words.ex: The festival showed a panoply of colorful costumes.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日展示了丰富多彩的服装。
words.en: A panoply is a complete or impressive collection of things or a splendid display.

words.ex: He saw a beautiful panorama from the mountain top.
words.ex_cn: 他从山顶看到了美丽的全景。
words.en: A panorama is a view of a wide area, or a description or study that presents all the different parts or aspects of a particular subject.

words.tr:
n. 哑剧；（英）圣诞童话剧
v. 打手势；演哑剧
words.ex: The children laughed at the clown's pantomime.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们笑了，因为小丑的哑剧表演。
words.en: Pantomime is a type of entertainment where performers express a story or represent characters through gestures and body movements without using speech.

words.ex: The Pan-American Games are held every four years.
words.ex_cn: 泛美运动会每四年举办一次。
words.en: relating to or involving all the countries of North, South, and Central America

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G5

words.tr: n. 时代错误；不合时代的事；过时的事或人
words.ex: The knight in the movie uses a smartphone, which is an anachronism.
words.ex_cn: 电影中的骑士使用智能手机，这是不合时宜的。
words.en: An anachronism is something that is out of place in terms of time or chronology, such as an object, a custom, or an idea that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it is placed.

words.tr:
n. 编年史；年代记
v. 按时间顺序记录
words.ex: He writes a chronicle of his daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他记录自己每天的生活。
words.en: A chronicle is a historical account of events arranged in chronological order, typically without analysis or interpretation.

words.tr: n. 年代学；年表；按年代次序的排列
words.ex: He wrote the chronology of ancient Rome.
words.ex_cn: 他写了古罗马的年代顺序。
words.en: Chronology is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.

words.tr: adj. 按时间先后顺序排列的
words.ex: The events are listed in chronological order.
words.ex_cn: 这些事件按时间顺序列出。
words.en: If things are described or shown in chronological order, they are described or shown in the order in which they happened.

words.ex: The two clocks synchronize automatically.
words.ex_cn: 这两座钟自动同时发生。
words.en: If you synchronize two activities, processes, or movements, or if you synchronize one activity, process, or movement with another, you cause them to happen at the same time and speed as each other.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G6

words.ex: She was diagnosed with kleptomania and started receiving treatment.
words.ex_cn: 她被诊断为盗窃癖并开始接受治疗。
words.en: Kleptomania is a mental disorder in which the person feels a strong, uncontrollable urge to steal items, often things they don't need or have little value.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr:
n. 疯子；狂人；狂热分子
adj. 疯狂的；狂热的
words.ex: The maniac screamed loudly in the street.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯子在街上大声喊叫。
words.en: A maniac is a person who has a very strong interest in something or behaves in a very wild or violent way.

words.ex: He has pyromania and loves to light fires.
words.ex_cn: 他有纵火癖，喜欢点火。
words.en: A mental disorder characterized by an irresistible impulse to start fires.

words.tr: adj. 发狂的；狂热的；疯狂的
words.ex: He had a maniacal glint in his eyes as he spoke about his new project.
words.ex_cn: 他谈起自己的新项目时，眼中闪烁着狂热的光芒。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as maniacal, you mean that it is extremely wild and often violent because they are mentally ill or very angry.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G7

words.ex: He looked up the word in an encyclopedia.
words.ex_cn: 他从百科全书中查找这个词。
words.en: An encyclopedia is a book or set of books giving information on many subjects or on many aspects of one subject and typically arranged alphabetically.

words.tr: adj. 整形外科的；矫形术的
words.ex: He visits the orthopedic doctor for his knee pain.
words.ex_cn: 他去看骨科医生治疗他的膝盖疼痛。
words.en: relating to the branch of medicine dealing with the correction of deformities of bones or muscles

words.tr: n. 施教者；好为人师的人；卖弄学问者
words.ex: The pedagogue taught children to read and write.
words.ex_cn: 这位教师教孩子们读书写字。
words.en: A pedagogue is a teacher, especially one who is strict or old-fashioned in their methods.

words.ex: The teacher learned new pedagogy from the workshop.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师从研讨会中学到了新的教学法。
words.en: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.

words.ex: The pediatrician checks the child's health every month.
words.ex_cn: 儿科医生每个月检查孩子的健康状况。
words.en: A pediatrician is a doctor who specializes in the care of children and their diseases.

words.ex: He became a doctor in pediatrics after years of study.
words.ex_cn: 经过多年的学习，他成为了儿科学医生。
words.en: Pediatrics is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, children, and adolescents.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G8

words.tr: n. 正牙医生；牙齿矫正医师
words.ex: He visits the orthodontist every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月都去看牙科正畸医生。
words.en: A dentist who is qualified to treat irregularities in the teeth and jaws.

words.ex: He learned proper orthography in elementary school.
words.ex_cn: 他在小学学习了正确的正字法。
words.en: Orthography is the conventional spelling system of a language.

words.tr: n. 整形外科医师（等于 orthopaedist）
words.ex: The orthopedist fixed his broken leg.
words.ex_cn: 这位整形外科医师治好了他断裂的腿。
words.en: An orthopedist is a doctor who specializes in the branch of medicine concerned with the correction or prevention of deformities, disorders, or injuries of the skeleton and associated structures.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.ex: He uses an unorthodox method to teach math.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种非传统的方法教数学。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour, beliefs, or customs as unorthodox, you mean that they are different from what is generally accepted.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G9

words.tr: n. 家谱学；系谱学；宗谱学；家谱（图）
words.ex: He is learning his family genealogy.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习自己的家族家谱。
words.en: Genealogy is the study of the history of families and the line of descent from their ancestors.

words.ex: The genesis of the story is a simple dream.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的起源是一个简单的梦。
words.en: The origin or mode of formation of something.

words.ex: The machine will homogenize the milk.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器会将牛奶均质化。
words.en: To homogenize something means to make it the same throughout, or to make it uniform.

words.tr: adj. 异种的；异质的；由不同成份形成的
words.ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级是多元的，有来自许多国家的学生。
words.en: A heterogeneous group consists of many different types of things or people.

words.ex: The mixture is homogeneous and looks the same throughout.
words.ex_cn: 这种混合物是均一的，看起来处处都一样。
words.en: Something that is homogeneous is uniform in nature or character throughout.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G10

words.ex: The barometer shows that the weather will be fine.
words.ex_cn: 晴雨表显示天气会很好。
words.en: A barometer is an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, used especially in forecasting the weather and determining altitude.

words.tr: n. 计时机；精密的时计；天文钟
words.ex: He uses a chronometer to measure time precisely.
words.ex_cn: 他使用精密计时器来精确测量时间。
words.en: A chronometer is a very accurate clock, especially one used for scientific purposes or for measuring time at sea.

words.ex: The diameter of the circle is 10 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的直径是10厘米。
words.en: A straight line passing from side to side through the center of a body or figure, especially a circle or sphere.

words.tr: n. 米；公尺；仪表；计量仪；
words.ex: The table is two meters long.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子两米长。
words.en: A meter is a unit of length in the metric system, equal to 100 centimeters. It can also refer to a device that measures and records the quantity, degree, or rate of something, such as electricity or gas.

words.ex: The car's odometer shows 50,000 miles.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的里程表显示50,000英里。
words.en: An odometer is an instrument in a vehicle that measures and displays the total distance that the vehicle has traveled.

words.ex: He uses a photometer to measure light intensity.
words.ex_cn: 他使用光度计来测量光强度。
words.en: A photometer is an instrument for measuring the intensity of light.

words.ex: The speedometer showed a steady increase in speed.
words.ex_cn: 速度计显示速度在稳步增加。
words.en: A speedometer is a device in a vehicle which shows how fast the vehicle is moving.

words.ex: The butterfly has perfect symmetry.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶有完美的对称性。
words.en: Symmetry is the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G11

words.tr: n. 对手；对立者；对抗者
words.ex: The antagonist in the story is a greedy king.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的反派是一个贪婪的国王。
words.en: An antagonist is someone who opposes another person.

words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.ex: The body makes an antibody to fight the virus.
words.ex_cn: 身体产生一种抗体来对抗病毒。
words.en: An antibody is a protein produced by the body's immune system when it detects harmful substances, called antigens. Each type of antibody is unique and defends the body against one specific type of antigen.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an antidote for the poison.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一种解毒剂来对抗毒药。
words.en: An antidote is a substance that counteracts the effects of poison or something harmful.

words.ex: He felt antipathy toward the loud neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对那个吵闹的邻居感到反感。
words.en: A deep-seated feeling of dislike; aversion.

words.ex: The doctor used antiseptic cream on the cut.
words.ex_cn: 医生在伤口上用了防腐药膏。
words.en: An antiseptic is a substance that prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an antitoxin to fight the poison.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一种抗毒素来对抗毒素。
words.en: An antitoxin is an antibody with the ability to neutralize a specific toxin.

words.ex: The antonym of 'hot' is 'cold'.
words.ex_cn: ‘hot’的反义词是‘cold’。
words.en: An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G12

words.ex: NASA is an acronym for National Aeronautics and Space Administration.
words.ex_cn: NASA 是美国国家航空航天局的缩写。
words.en: An acronym is a word formed from the initial letters of the words in a phrase, especially when this is used as a name.

words.tr: n. 同形（同音）异义词；同名异物
words.ex: The words 'bear' and 'bare' are homonyms.
words.ex_cn: “bear”和“bare”这两个词是同音异义词。
words.en: A homonym is a word that is pronounced the same as another word but differs in meaning. The words may be spelled the same, such as 'rose' (flower) and 'rose' (past tense of rise), or differently, such as 'carat', 'caret', and 'carrot'.

words.ex: The word 'buzz' is an example of onomatopoeia.
words.ex_cn: 单词'buzz'是拟声的一个例子。
words.en: The formation of a word from a sound associated with what is named.

words.ex: He writes books under a pseudonym.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔名写书。
words.en: A pseudonym is a name that someone, especially a writer, uses instead of their real name.

words.ex: The synonym of 'happy' is 'glad'.
words.ex_cn: ‘happy’的同义词是‘glad’。
words.en: A synonym is a word or phrase that means exactly or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language.

words.ex: He posted an anonymous comment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在网上发布了一条匿名评论。
words.en: If you remain anonymous when you do something, you do not let people know that you were the person who did it.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G13

words.tr: n. 皮肤病学家；皮肤科医生
words.ex: He visited a dermatologist for his skin rash.
words.ex_cn: 他因为皮肤疹去看皮肤科医生。
words.en: A dermatologist is a doctor who specializes in the study, diagnosis, and treatment of skin disorders and diseases.

words.ex: The dermis contains blood vessels and nerve endings.
words.ex_cn: 真皮包含血管和神经末梢。
words.en: The dermis is the thick layer of living tissue below the epidermis that forms the true skin, containing blood capillaries, nerve endings, sweat glands, hair follicles, and other structures.

words.ex: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin.
words.ex_cn: 表皮是皮肤的最外层。
words.en: The epidermis is the outer layer of the skin of an animal, which serves as a protective barrier against the environment.

words.tr: n. 动物标本剥制者；剥制师
words.ex: The taxidermist skillfully preserved the deer's hide.
words.ex_cn: 剥制师熟练地保存了鹿的皮。
words.en: A taxidermist is a person whose job is to prepare the skins of dead animals and fill them with a special material so that they look like living animals and can be displayed.

words.tr:
adj. 皮下注射的；皮下的
n. 皮下注射；皮下注射器
words.ex: The nurse used a hypodermic needle to give him a shot.
words.ex_cn: 护士用皮下注射针给他打了一针。
words.en: A hypodermic needle or syringe is a medical instrument with a hollow needle used to inject substances into the body or extract fluids from it.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G14

words.ex: He is learning agronomy at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习农学。
words.en: Agronomy is the science of soil management and crop production.

words.tr: n. 爱吃的人；美食家；讲究饮食的人
words.ex: As a gastronome, she travels the world to taste different cuisines.
words.ex_cn: 作为一个美食家，她环游世界品尝不同的菜肴。
words.en: A gastronome is a person who enjoys and knows a lot about good food and drink.

words.ex: His dishonesty became his nemesis.
words.ex_cn: 他的不诚实成了他的天谴。
words.en: Someone's nemesis is a person or thing that is very difficult for them to defeat.

words.ex: He uses an astronomical telescope to watch stars.
words.ex_cn: 他用一架天文望远镜观察星星。
words.en: If you describe an amount, especially the cost of something as astronomical, you are emphasizing that it is very large indeed.

words.ex: The economic situation is getting worse.
words.ex_cn: 经济状况正在恶化。
words.en: Economic means concerned with the organization of the money, industry, and trade of a country, region, or society.

words.ex: This car is economical because it uses little fuel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车很经济，因为它耗油少。
words.en: Using money, resources, or time in a careful and effective way.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G15

words.ex: He wrapped the candy in cellophane.
words.ex_cn: 他用玻璃纸包了糖果。
words.en: A thin, transparent sheet made of regenerated cellulose, used mainly as a wrapping material.

words.tr:
v. 想要；
adj. 花哨的；昂贵的；
n. 爱好；
words.ex: I fancy a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 我想要一杯茶。
words.en: If you describe something as fancy, you mean that it is special, unusual, or elaborate, often because it has a lot of decoration or is very expensive.

words.ex: The child loves to play with fantasy stories about dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢玩关于龙的幻想故事。
words.en: A fantasy is a pleasant situation or event that you imagine, which is unlikely to happen.

words.ex: The phantom appeared in the mist near the old house.
words.ex_cn: 幻影出现在老房子附近的薄雾中。
words.en: A phantom is a ghost or a figment of the imagination.

words.ex: The rainbow is a natural phenomenon.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹是一种自然现象。
words.en: A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist, especially something that is unusual or interesting.

words.ex: Her performance was phenomenal.
words.ex_cn: 她的表现非常非凡。
words.en: If you describe something as phenomenal, you think it is extremely good or impressive.

words.ex: The movie was fantastic!
words.ex_cn: 这部电影极好！
words.en: If you describe something as fantastic, you are emphasizing that you think it is very good or that you like it a lot.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G16

words.ex: The doctor used diathermy to treat the patient's muscle strain.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用透热疗法治疗患者的肌肉拉伤。
words.en: Diathermy is a medical and physical therapy technique that uses high-frequency electric currents to produce heat within body tissues to promote healing and reduce pain.

words.ex: He checked the thermometer to see the temperature.
words.ex_cn: 他看了温度计来查看温度。
words.en: A thermometer is an instrument for measuring and indicating temperature.

words.ex: He set the thermostat to 22 degrees.
words.ex_cn: 他把恒温器调到了22度。
words.en: A thermostat is a device that automatically regulates temperature, or that activates a device when the temperature reaches a certain point.

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.ex: The sun produces energy through thermonuclear reactions.
words.ex_cn: 太阳通过热核反应产生能量。
words.en: Thermonuclear refers to the process or phenomena that involve the fusion of atomic nuclei at very high temperatures, as in the sun or in a hydrogen bomb.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G17

words.ex: He is the protagonist in the story.
words.ex_cn: 他是故事中的主角。
words.en: The main character in a story, play, film, etc., especially the one who is good or who the audience is expected to support.

words.ex: The two countries signed a protocol to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项停止战争的协议。
words.en: A protocol is a set of rules or a system of rules about the correct way to act in formal situations.

words.ex: The cell contains protoplasm.
words.ex_cn: 细胞中含有原生质。
words.en: The colorless material comprising the living part of a cell, including the cytoplasm, nucleus, and other organelles.

words.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
words.ex_cn: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。
words.en: A prototype is the first or original example of something that has been or will be copied or developed; it is a model or preliminary version.

words.ex: The protozoan moves in water with tiny hairs.
words.ex_cn: 这个原生动物用细小的毛发在水中移动。
words.en: A protozoan is a single-celled organism that is considered to be an animal, typically microscopic and found in water.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G18

words.ex: His calmness is the antithesis of her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他的冷静是她愤怒的反面。
words.en: The antithesis of something is its exact opposite.

words.ex: They called him 'Quick Feet' as an epithet.
words.ex_cn: 他们用‘快脚’作为他的绰号。
words.en: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase added to or substituted for a person's name, often to describe a characteristic or quality.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

words.ex: His thesis is that exercise improves memory.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是锻炼能改善记忆力。
words.en: A thesis is a long piece of writing based on your own ideas and research that you do as part of a university degree, especially a higher degree such as a PhD.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G19

words.tr: n. [植]紫菀属植物；星状体; n. （Aster）人名；（德、意、捷）阿斯特尔
words.ex: He saw an aster in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他在花园里看到一朵星花。
words.en: A plant of the genus Aster, which includes many species of flowering plants known for their star-shaped flower heads.

words.tr:
n. 星号
v. 给…注上星号
words.ex: She put an asterisk next to the word.
words.ex_cn: 她在那个词旁边加了一个星号。
words.en: An asterisk is a symbol (*) used in text to indicate a footnote or to highlight something important.

words.ex: The asteroid flew past Earth safely.
words.ex_cn: 这颗小行星安全地从地球旁飞过。
words.en: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun. Large numbers of these, ranging enormously in size, are found between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, though some have more eccentric orbits.

words.ex: The astrologer told her fortune with stars.
words.ex_cn: 占星家用星星为她算命。
words.en: An astrologer is a person who studies the movements and positions of the stars and planets in the belief that they influence human affairs and natural phenomena.

words.ex: The astronaut walked on the moon.
words.ex_cn: 这名宇航员在月球上行走。
words.en: An astronaut is a person who is trained to travel in a spacecraft.

words.ex: The astronomer looks at stars through a telescope.
words.ex_cn: 这位天文学家通过望远镜观察星星。
words.en: An astronomer is a scientist who studies celestial bodies such as planets, stars, and galaxies.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

chapters.name: 第二章 认识希腊词根 G20

words.tr: n. 变位词（相同字母异序词）
words.ex: He solved the anagram quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解出了这个字谜。
words.en: An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.

words.tr: n. 制图员；地图绘制员
words.ex: The cartographer drew a map of the island.
words.ex_cn: 这位制图师画了一张岛屿的地图。
words.en: A cartographer is a person who draws or produces maps.

words.ex: The detective spent hours trying to solve the cryptogram.
words.ex_cn: 侦探花了几个小时试图解开这个密码。
words.en: A cryptogram is a text written in code.

words.ex: The doctor ordered an electrocardiogram to check the patient's heart function.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张心电图检查单，以检查患者的心脏功能。
words.en: A record or display of a person's heartbeat produced by electrocardiography.

words.ex: He wrote a short epigram about love.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一首关于爱情的短小警句。
words.en: A short poem or sentence that expresses something such as a feeling or idea in a short and clever or funny way.

words.ex: He uses graphite to draw pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他用石墨画画。
words.en: Graphite is a soft, black form of carbon that is used in pencils and as a lubricant.

words.tr: n. 交织字母；花押字（某人姓名首字母构成的图案，缝制于个人衣物等上）
words.ex: She sewed her monogram on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上缝上了她的姓名首字母图案。
words.en: A monogram is a motif made by overlapping or combining two or more letters or other graphemes to form one symbol.

words.ex: He wrote a monograph on ancient Chinese pottery.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一本关于中国古代陶器的专著。
words.en: A monograph is a detailed written study or report on a specific subject or aspect of a subject, especially by a single author.

words.ex: The stenographer wrote down every word in court.
words.ex_cn: 速记员记下了法庭里的每一句话。
words.en: A stenographer is a person who specializes in taking dictation in shorthand.

words.ex: The story had a graphic description of the battle.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事对战斗的描述非常生动。
words.en: A graphic is a visual representation of data or information, such as a chart, diagram, or picture.

words.tr: adj. 排字上的；印刷上的
words.ex: The typo was a typographical error.
words.ex_cn: 这个拼写错误是一个排版错误。
words.en: Relating to the arrangement, appearance, or style of printed matter.

chapters.name: 第三章 （1）拉丁前缀 G1

words.ex: The abrasion on his knee hurt a lot.
words.ex_cn: 他膝盖上的擦伤非常疼。
words.en: An abrasion is an area on a person's body where the skin has been scraped off.

words.ex: His avocation is painting on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他的业余爱好是周末画画。
words.en: An avocation is an activity that you do because you are interested in it, rather than as your main job.

words.ex: The king decided to abdicate in favor of his son.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定退位，让位给他的儿子。
words.en: If a king or queen abdicates, he or she gives up being king or queen.

words.ex: The aliens abduct the man at night.
words.ex_cn: 外星人在晚上绑架了那个男人。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force or deception; kidnap.

words.ex: She abhors violence.
words.ex_cn: 她憎恶暴力。
words.en: If you abhor something, you hate it very much, especially because you think it is immoral or disgusting.

words.ex: He absconded with the money last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚携款逃跑了。
words.en: If someone absconds from somewhere, they leave there quickly and secretly because they have something to hide or are afraid of being caught.

words.ex: The judge will absolve him of all charges.
words.ex_cn: 法官将免除他所有的罪名。
words.en: If someone is absolved of blame, responsibility, or a sin, they are formally forgiven for it or declared free from it.

words.tr: v. 戒绝；弃权；自我克制
words.ex: He abstains from eating sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他戒食糖。
words.en: If you abstain from something, you deliberately do not do it or have it, especially something you like or enjoy which might be considered bad for you.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.ex: He made an abrupt stop at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 他在红灯前突然停了下来。
words.en: If something happens abruptly, it happens suddenly and unexpectedly.

words.tr: v. 吸收；“absorb”的现在分词； adj. 吸引人的；
words.ex: The sponge is absorbing water.
words.ex_cn: 海绵正在吸收水。
words.en: If something is absorbing, it is very interesting and holds your attention completely.

words.ex: He is averse to changing his routine.
words.ex_cn: 他反对改变自己的日常安排。
words.en: If you say that someone is averse to something, you mean they dislike it or have a strong opposition to it.

chapters.name: 第三章 （1）拉丁前缀 G2

words.tr:
n. 拥护者；信徒
adj. 黏附…的
words.ex: He is an adherent of the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 他是这项新政策的拥护者。
words.en: An adherent is someone who supports a particular party, person, or set of ideas.

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: He faced his adversary in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 他在决赛中对阵对手。
words.en: An adversary is someone who you are competing with, or who is opposing you or what you are trying to do.

words.ex: He adapted to the new school quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快就适应了新学校。
words.en: To make suitable to or fit for a specific use or situation.

words.ex: The two rooms adjoin each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两个房间彼此相邻。
words.en: If one room, place, or object adjoins another, they are next to each other.

words.ex: The meeting will adjourn at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议将在下午5点休会。
words.en: If a meeting or trial is adjourned, or if it adjourns, it is stopped for a short time.

words.tr: adj. 上瘾了的；入了迷的
words.ex: He is addicted to video games.
words.ex_cn: 他沉迷于电子游戏。
words.en: If you are addicted to something, you cannot stop doing it or using it, even though it may be harmful to you.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

chapters.name: 第三章 （1）拉丁前缀 G4

words.tr: n. 前情；先行词；祖先；经历；“antecedent”的复数
words.ex: The antecedents of the conflict go back to last year.
words.ex_cn: 这场冲突的前情可以追溯到去年。
words.en: An antecedent is a thing or event that existed before or logically precedes another.

words.ex: The guests waited in the anteroom before being called for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 客人们在被叫去吃饭之前在前厅等候。
words.en: A small room leading to a main one, often used as a waiting area.

words.tr:
n. 验尸；尸检；事后调查
adj. 死后的；死后发生的
words.ex: The doctor did a postmortem to find the cause of death.
words.ex_cn: 医生做了尸检以查明死因。
words.en: An examination of a dead body to determine the cause of death or the character and extent of changes produced by disease.

words.tr: n. 附言；附录；补充说明
words.ex: He added a postscript to his letter.
words.ex_cn: 他在信后加了一段附言。
words.en: A postscript is a note appended to a finished letter, article, or book.

words.ex: He antedated the contract by one week.
words.ex_cn: 他把合同的日期提前了一周。
words.en: To be of an earlier date than something else; to precede in time.

words.ex: He postdated the check to next month.
words.ex_cn: 他把支票的日期写成下个月。
words.en: To write a date on a document that is later than the actual date.

words.tr: phrase. 午前的，上午的（用于12小时制时间表示，缩写为 a.m.）
words.ex: The meeting is scheduled for 10:00 ante meridiem.
words.ex_cn: 会议安排在上午10点。
words.en: before noon

words.tr: phrase. 中午之后：表示在中午之后。
words.ex: The meeting is scheduled for 3:00 PM (post meridiem).
words.ex_cn: 会议定于下午3:00（中午之后）举行。
words.en: Post meridiem is used to represent the time from noon to midnight.

words.tr:
n. 研究生；
adj. 大学毕业后的；
words.ex: He is a postgraduate at Beijing University.
words.ex_cn: 他是北京大学的一名研究生。
words.en: A postgraduate is a student who continues studying after obtaining a first degree, usually in order to obtain a higher qualification.

chapters.name: 第三章 （1）拉丁前缀 G6

words.tr: adj. 每二百年发生一次的；
words.ex: The bicentennial celebration marked 200 years since the country's founding.
words.ex_cn: 二百年庆典纪念了该国建国200周年。
words.en: A bicentennial is the two-hundredth anniversary of a significant event.

words.ex: The child drew a semicircle on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在纸上画了一个半圆。
words.en: A semicircle is half of a circle, or something that has the shape of half a circle.

words.ex: The line bisects the angle into two equal parts.
words.ex_cn: 这条线将角平分为两个相等的部分。
words.en: To divide something into two equal parts.

words.tr: adj. 两院制的；有参众两院的
words.ex: The country has a bicameral parliament.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个两院制议会。
words.en: A bicameral legislature is one that is divided into two separate assemblies, chambers, or houses.

words.tr:
adj. 每两年一次的；二年生的
n. 二年生植物
words.ex: The biennial art show attracts many visitors.
words.ex_cn: 每两年一次的艺术展吸引了很多参观者。
words.en: Happening every two years or lasting for two years.

words.tr:
adj. 两月一次的；每月两次的
adv. 两月一次地；每月两次地
words.ex: The magazine is published bimonthly.
words.ex_cn: 这本杂志每两月出版一次。
words.en: Happening or produced every two months or twice a month.

words.tr: adj. 每半年的；半年一次的
words.ex: The company holds semiannual meetings to update employees on recent developments.
words.ex_cn: 公司每半年举行一次会议，向员工通报最新进展。
words.en: occurring or payable twice each year

words.tr: adv. 每半月一次; adj. 每半个月一次的; n. 半月刊
words.ex: The company issues a semimonthly newsletter to keep employees informed.
words.ex_cn: 公司每半月发行一份新闻简报，以保持员工的信息更新。
words.en: occurring or produced twice a month.

words.ex: The two countries signed a bilateral agreement.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项双边协议。
words.en: Involving or affecting two parties, countries, etc.

words.tr: adj. 两种语言的；用两种语言的；
words.ex: He is a bilingual student who speaks English and Spanish.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个会说英语和西班牙语的双语学生。
words.en: A bilingual person is someone who can speak two languages equally well.

words.tr: adj. 两党的；代表两党的
words.ex: The bill passed with bipartisan support.
words.ex_cn: 该法案获得了两党的支持。
words.en: Involving the agreement or cooperation of two political parties that usually oppose each other's policies.

words.tr: adj. 半清醒的；半意识的
words.ex: She was semiconscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，她处于半清醒状态。
words.en: Partially conscious; not fully aware of one's surroundings.

words.tr: adj. （房屋）半独立式的，与他屋共用一墙的
words.ex: They live in a semi-detached house near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在公园附近的一栋半独立式房子里。
words.en: A semi-detached house is a house that is joined to another house on one side only.

words.ex: He works as a semi-skilled worker in a factory.
words.ex_cn: 他在工厂里做半熟练工。
words.en: Semi-skilled work or workers have some skills but not enough to be considered skilled.

chapters.name: 第三章 （1）拉丁前缀 G8

words.tr:
n. 起义者；叛乱者；造反者
adj. 叛乱的；起义的
words.ex: The insurgent attacked the village at night.
words.ex_cn: 叛乱分子在夜里袭击了村庄。
words.en: An insurgent is a person who rises in active revolt against an established authority or government.

words.ex: Water causes erosion of the soil.
words.ex_cn: 水会导致土壤腐蚀。
words.en: The process by which the surface of the earth is worn away by the action of water, glaciers, winds, waves, etc.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.ex: They want to immigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他们想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To come to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: The government raised the excise on tobacco.
words.ex_cn: 政府提高了烟草的货物税。
words.en: Excise is a tax that is charged on goods produced within a country, or on goods that are brought into a country from abroad, especially on goods such as alcohol and tobacco. It can also refer to the act of cutting out or removing something, especially in a surgical operation.

words.ex: The artist incised the design into the wood.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家将设计雕刻在木头上。
words.en: To cut into a surface with a sharp tool; to carve or engrave.

words.ex: The museum will exhibit ancient coins next month.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆下个月将展览古钱币。
words.en: To exhibit something means to show it in a public place so that people can go to see it. It can also mean to show a particular quality, ability, or type of behavior.

words.ex: The medicine helps inhibit pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于抑制疼痛。
words.en: If something inhibits an event or process, it prevents it or slows it down.

words.ex: The body expels waste through the kidneys.
words.ex_cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物。
words.en: If someone is expelled from a school or organization, they are officially told to leave because they have behaved badly or broken the rules.

words.ex: The danger impels him to act quickly.
words.ex_cn: 危险驱使他迅速行动。
words.en: If something impels you to do something, it makes you feel very strongly that you must do it.

words.ex: The hot weather enervates him.
words.ex_cn: 炎热的天气让他感到乏力。
words.en: If something enervates you, it makes you feel weak and lacking in energy.

words.tr: v. 使牵连其中；涉及；暗示；指明起因
words.ex: The evidence may implicate him in the crime.
words.ex_cn: 证据可能使他牵连进这起犯罪中。
words.en: To show or suggest that someone is involved in something illegal or morally wrong.

words.ex: He will impugn the witness's honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他将质疑证人的诚实性。
words.en: To impugn means to challenge as false or questionable; to cast doubt upon.

words.ex: The man was incarcerated for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 这个人因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: If people are incarcerated, they are kept in a prison or other place.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.tr: adj. 包容的；包含全部费用的；
words.ex: The school is inclusive and welcomes all students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校是包容的，欢迎所有学生。
words.en: Inclusive is used to describe something that is designed to include all types of people, things, or ideas, and to treat them all fairly and equally.

chapters.name: 第三章 （1）拉丁前缀 G10

words.ex: He joins extracurricular activities after school.
words.ex_cn: 他放学后参加课外活动。
words.en: Extracurricular activities are those that fall outside the realm of the normal curriculum of school or university education, performed by students. Extracurricular activities exist at all levels of education, from 4th-6th, junior high/high school, college and university education.

words.ex: The extraneous noise made it hard to concentrate.
words.ex_cn: 那些无关的噪音让人难以集中注意力。
words.en: Something that is extraneous is not relevant or essential to the subject you are dealing with.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
